text.p: Following are the highlights of an interview which Finance Minister P. Chidambaram granted to Reuters at the weekend:
* Chidambaram will discuss price stability, bank credit and a surge in foreign exchange inflows with the Reserve Bank of India on Monday.
* "It is necessary to ensure that adequate credit is made available to industry, to agriculture for productive purposes."

* There is no question of allowing the rupee to depreciate. The foreign exchange market must determine the level of the rupee. The central bank is concerned that there should be no volatility in the market.
* If imports rise, as the government expects, some of the inflow of U.S. dollars will be consumed.
* Easing restrictions on consumer goods imports is an option to be decided in the government's Export-Import policy, due to be announced on March 31.

* India's situation cannot be compared to that of Mexico, which has had to grapple with debt crises, as India's short-term debt as a share of total debt is small and it does not have dollar-denominated bonds.
* The mounting oil pool deficit has to be addressed by the Petroleum Ministry. The deficit is outside the budget.
* Any impact on inflation from a rise in petroleum product prices will depend on "whether there is a price increase, what is the price increase and when it has come".
* The fiscal deficit and inflation have to be brought under control before the rupee can be made fully convertible on capital account.
* Industry will be more competitive if interest rates are lower.
* A report by IMF economists saying India could face a debt crisis unless deeper cuts were made in the fiscal deficit is "out of a text book".
* U.S. credit rating agency Moody's was "wrong" in taking an unfavourable outlook on India's sovereign rating.
* A weaker rupee would help exporters but hurt many others.
* Imports and exports are expected to pick up in 1997.
* The Commerce Ministry could help exports by meeting representatives of key sectors including shrimps, garments, tea, engineering goods, gems and jewellery.
* The budget allows capital goods in the power sector to be imported with a 20 percent duty. "What more does the investor want?"
* The government is confident it will reach its tax revenue targets for 1997/98 (April-March) despite tax rate cuts.
* The government must reward savers and tax spenders.
* Political parties are bound to find fault with aspects of the budget, but the overall perception is positive. "I believe the budget will pass."
-- Nelson Graves, New Delhi newsroom +91-11 301 2024
